newsitem.title: USA: Fed suggests banks be allowed longer check holds.
newsitem.headline: Fed suggests banks be allowed longer check holds.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Reserve Board Wednesday recommended that banks be allowed to place longer holds on check deposits even though a staff report said there was no way to tell if that would reduce check fraud.

The board unanimously adopted a report to Congress that recommended lawmakers change current banking rules to allow institutions to place holds on local check deposits for up to three days instead of the current two.

"Increasing the maximum permissible hold period for local checks by one business day would allow depository banks to receive more than 80 percent of all local returned checks before they would be required to make funds available to their customers," the report said.
The report said that only 48 percent of local returned checks are received by a depository institution within the current two-day limit on check holds.
A 1987 law limited the time a bank can withhold funds from depositors and Congress asked the Fed last year to study whether the limit has increased check fraud.
But the staff said that because of a lack of data before the law went into effect, there was no way to determine whether shorter check hold periods contributed to check fraud.
Federal Reserve board members said they were reluctantly supporting the recommendation to allow longer hold periods.
"I didn't easily come to that decision," said Governor Edward Kelley, echoing the views voiced by other board members. "The third day is the crucial day."
The report noted that many banks make funds available to depositors earlier than required by law and that many banks apply a longer period on a case-by-case basis.
